cards.explanation: The answer is tenderly, friends. The words are “Speak tenderly to Jerusalem, and proclaim to her…” Not a lecture, not a scolding, just a gentle voice. After years in the back of a junk drawer, I can tell you that gentle is the voice you want to hear.

The answer is False. The text says her forced labor has been completed and “her iniquity has been pardoned.” Nothing is sitting on a shelf waiting for her, friends. Pardoned means done, and this is good news from the start.

The answer is in the wilderness. The voice says, “Prepare the way for the LORD in the wilderness…” It's not a spot with a nice view or a gift shop. The highway goes in the desert, friends, and the work starts right there.
The answer is lifted. The text says, “Every valley shall be lifted up…” The low spots come up so the road is ready. It's like filling the world's biggest pothole, and I'd pay to watch that crew.
The answer is False. The valleys are lifted up, but every mountain and hill is “made low.” High ones come down and low ones go up, friends. That's how you end up with a smooth road.

The answer is the glory of the LORD. The voice says, “And the glory of the LORD will be revealed…” After all that talk of valleys and mountains, here comes the big reveal. The text says all humanity together will see it.

The answer is all humanity together. The text says, “…all humanity together will see it.” Nobody is left out and nobody gets a private showing, friends. Everybody sees it at the same time, like one giant crowd looking up at the same sky.

The answer is that the grass withers and the flowers fall. When the breath of the LORD blows on them, “The grass withers and the flowers fall…” It's a blunt picture of how brief we are, friends. I'll say it: I've seen my own edges go soft, and the picture fits.

The answer is forever. “The grass withers and the flowers fall, but the word of our God stands forever.” The people are called grass, and their glory is like the flowers of the field (Isaiah 40:6 and 7). But the word of our God stands. That's the part to hold onto, friends.

The answer is False. The herald is told, “Raise your voice loudly, O Jerusalem, herald of good news.” Then comes “Lift it up, do not be afraid!” This message is meant to be heard, friends, so don't hold it in.
The answer is “Here is your God!” The herald is told to say it to the cities of Judah. It's the whole message in four words, friends. I think that's why it's worth shouting from a mountain.

The answer is that His arm establishes His rule. The verse says, “Behold, the Lord GOD comes with might, and His arm establishes His rule.” His arm is how He sets up His rule. That's strength with a purpose, friends, and that verse has weight.

The answer is shepherd. “He tends His flock like a shepherd…” The One who comes with might is also the One who tends, friends. That's a surprising pair, and it's all in the same short stretch of verses.

The answer is close to His heart. The verse says, “He gathers the lambs in His arms and carries them close to His heart.” The lambs aren't made to walk it alone, friends. They get carried right up against Him.
The answer is False. The verse says, “He gently leads the nursing ewes.” That's how this shepherd treats them, friends. After all that might in verse 10, this is a soft side of the same Lord GOD.
